At Badr Allah answers the Prophet's prayer with angels; he takes ransom for captives on Abu Bakr's advice, weeps at the punishment shown for it, and booty is made lawful.
Before Badr the Prophet consults his companions and Sa'd b. Ubada pledges to follow him anywhere; a captured water-carrier is beaten, and the Prophet marks where each enemy will fall.
After Badr Ibn Mas'ud finds Abu Jahl dying, struck down by the two sons of Afra, and Abu Jahl laments that farmers killed him.
Hatib's letter to the Meccans was seized; the Prophet accepted his explanation, refused Umar's wish to kill him as he fought at Badr, and said he would not enter Hell.
The Prophet showed where each of Badr's dead would fall, then called to the Quraysh dead in the well, telling Umar they heard him but could not reply.
Abu Dharr swore that 'These two adversaries who dispute about their Lord' concerns Hamza, Ali and Ubaida, who came out at Badr against Utba, Shaiba and Walid.
